Rule: A DAAD letter of motivation is at most one page after proofreading: "At the end, your letter of motivation should comprise not more than one page."

DAAD publishes a content list, not an order: questions a (professional goal and sector), b (contribution to home-country development, facts and figures welcome), c (why this programme and which courses), d (why you) — and says "Not all of the above questions have to be addressed!" and "Do not include the outline or the questions in your text."
A DAAD letter does not open by repeating the CV: "Do not start your letter of motivation by repeating your CV."
DAAD register: "Avoid all kind of platitudes, flowery phrases and flattery. Deal with your topics in a reflective and factual way. Do not campaign for your beliefs."

DAAD prescribes no letter formalities: the advice sheet names no date, addressee, salutation, sign-off or signature; the only shape rules are the one-page limit and the composed outline. (Finding of absence; the separate hand-signature rule for EPOS is L-027.)

uni-assist describes the letter of motivation as "usually one or two pages long" and as explaining why this university, this course and why you are qualified; the university, not uni-assist, sets any further requirement.

TUM Informatics M.Sc.: the "schriftliche Begründung" is in English, at most two DIN-A4 pages, and argues the applicant's special commitment (Leistungsbereitschaft) through programme-specific training, internships, stays abroad or extra study, with evidence attached where applicable.

TUM Informatics scores the letter 0–24 on two criteria, the second of which is structural: "Strukturierte Darstellung des Zusammenhangs zwischen persönlicher Eignung und Inhalten des Studiengangs" — so the letter must visibly pair each personal qualification with a programme content.

TUM Informatics requires a declaration that the letter and essay were written "selbständig und ohne fremde Hilfe" with borrowed ideas marked as such (§2.3.5) — an authorship attestation attached to the letter.

ETH Zurich: the letter is "approximately one A4 page in the language of instruction of the chosen programme" and each programme's own requirements "are automatically displayed in the application form according to degree programme" — the form, not a general guide, is the source of the shape.

ETH Mathematics M.Sc.: the letter must "state and explain your choice of potential courses, areas of specialisation and supervisors for project work" — naming courses and prospective supervisors is required, not merely tolerated.

University of Vienna Data Science M.Sc.: the "letter of motivation" is a fixed form — a table of degrees (type, major, GPA, graduation date, university, thesis title) followed by numbered questions with per-answer character caps (1000/1000/500/200/1000/200/200); there is no free letter at all.

University of Vienna Data Science: the fit question explicitly invites named specifics — "What topics/research groups/modules may be of particular interest to you?" — capped at 500 characters, i.e. two or three named items, not a paragraph.

Utrecht University motivation statement: the template opens with three header fields — Name, UU student number, Master's programme — then six guiding questions in this order: why this programme and why Utrecht; experience demonstrating interest; most interesting subject areas and why; evidence of the required qualities; fit with career or research ambitions; reflection on academic achievements.
Binding or advisory: advisory (template optional: "you may also upload your own document")

Rule: Utrecht: "Please write this statement in the language of your chosen programme, or programme track/specialisation" and "In the Netherlands a motivation statement is generally one to two pages."

Leiden Psychology clinical specialisations: the mandatory form pre-prints the salutation "Dear members of the Admissions Committee," and the sign-off "Sincerely," — one of only two prescribed salutation-and-closing formulas found (the other is UFMG's Brazilian template, M-101); the applicant writes only the body.
Scope: Leiden University (Master in Psychology, clinical specialisations)

Rule: Leiden clinical Psychology: "a concise letter of approximately 400 words. NB. an exceedance of more than 10 percent of this word count eliminates the possibility of an excellent score on this selection criterium."
Scope: Leiden University (Master in Psychology, clinical specialisations)

Rule: Leiden clinical Psychology asks for a concrete thesis idea inside the letter: "Give an example of a topic (research question) for your master's thesis that you would like and why." Assessed on "quality and structure of the reasoning", programme connection, and "grammar, language and style".
Scope: Leiden University (Master in Psychology, clinical specialisations)

Rule: Groningen requires a letter of motivation only for its selective master's programmes (listed by faculty) and asks it to explain why you apply, why you are a good candidate, what you expect, and what you wish to achieve during and after; Law programmes cap it at 650 words.

Uppsala: the statement of purpose "is usually one page (c. 400 words) long" and describes why you apply, your expectations, relevant experience and what you hope to achieve as a graduate; some programmes take it as a field in the application summary sheet, others as a separate document.

Aalto School of Engineering (2019 guidance) frames the letter as answers to seven questions ending with "Why do you want to study at Aalto University and in Finland?" — a why-country slot inside a university (not scholarship) letter.

Sciences Po master's: the letter is typed into "la rubrique dédiée du dossier de candidature" (an online field), one per programme, in the programme's language, within the word cap shown in the dossier (the news page says "en maximum 1 000 mots").
Source (tier): T1 admissions page + T1 news page (17 Nov 2025)

Rule: Sciences Po lists four things the letter must show, in this order: parcours (precise elements of personality and background that lead to Sciences Po), intérêts académiques (which elements of the offer attract you — "maquette, objectifs pédagogiques"), adéquation professionnelle (the professional project and how the programme serves it), contribution (what you bring to Sciences Po, the programme and the cohort).

Sciences Po scores form as well as content: readers value "lettres soignées" on "le fond (clarté des idées, structure des arguments)" and "la forme (orthographe, paragraphes…)", and the letter "devra faire preuve d'authenticité et de sincérité".

French letter formalities (Campus France Minsk guidance): contact details top-left (nom, prénom, adresse, téléphone, mail); place and date top-right, then the addressee's name and function if known; an "Objet:" line such as "Demande d'admission en … pour la rentrée de …"; salutation "Madame, Monsieur," or "Comité de sélection des candidatures pour le diplôme de …" when the reader is unknown, "Monsieur X"/"Madame Y" when known; "Une formule de politesse est un passage obligé".
Source (tier): T2 Campus France office slide deck (mixes study and internship letters; cites l'Etudiant)

Rule: French opening: the first paragraph states the applicant's current or imminent diploma and names the programme applied for ("Je serai titulaire du … en juin 2023 et mon projet est d'intégrer votre master 1 …"); the middle relates parcours and competences to the diploma; the close restates motivation and suitability. Avoid "toujours rêvé" without proof and an over-familiar tone.
Source (tier): T2 Campus France office slide deck

Rule: Mon Master: the lettre de motivation is a per-formation requirement, listed in each application's details under "Mes candidatures" (alongside language test, research project, grades); the national guide itself prescribes no shape.
Source (tier): T1 Mon Master FAQ (search excerpt; guide PDF read: no letter rule)

Rule: Politecnico di Milano: the motivation letter is "a brief essay" (their words), optional but "can improve your chances", max two pages each, in English or Italian, and "If you apply to 2 courses, please write 2 different motivation letters … and combine them into one pdf".

Charles University FSV: "We do not have a set template for the motivation letters, and the form is mostly free"; it asks why this field, why FSV UK and this programme, why a field change, and "What shaped you?" — and warns that an AI letter hitting "all the expected buzzwords" is not what they want: "we want to hear your voice".
Charles University International Security Studies (2021 record): "Motivation 5 points" of a 1–10 ranking built from the submitted documents — the letter is half the score.

HSE Math of Machine Learning: letter of motivation "describing your reasons for applying in the context of your long-term career goals and background (no more than 1 page, A4)", worth 5 of 100 portfolio points; HSE letters may be in Russian or English.

Open Doors (Russia): the motivation letter is typed or pasted into a portfolio form field — no upload — and the "recommended structure" is given inside the participant account: scientific and career goals, professional achievements, reasons for the chosen subject area, motivation to study in Russia.

Nazarbayev University distinguishes three documents and expects the right one: a personal statement "is more about who you are", a motivation letter "is more about what you want to do … usually forward-looking and longer", and an essay answers a set topic shown on the application's "Essays" page; all are uploaded as PDF/JPEG ≤5 MB.

UNAM (Nursing master's) carta de exposición de motivos is a real letter: place-and-date line ("Ciudad de México a…"), "Asunto: Carta de exposición de motivos", addressed to the "Comité Académico del Programa" with "Presente", body in free format within two pages, closing "ATENTAMENTE", then the applicant's name and signature.
Scope: UNAM (Programa de Maestría y Doctorado en Enfermería)

Rule: UNAM (Nursing): the body opens with a data block (name, nationality, address, occupation, degree and university, other studies, prior research/thesis) and the admission route, then develops motives in three labelled kinds — PERSONALES, PROFESIONALES, DISCIPLINARES — then optional complementary information.
Universidad de Chile (Magíster en Estudios Internacionales): "Carta de intención, de una extensión máxima de 500 palabras, en que manifieste las razones que lo impulsan a desarrollar el magíster".

Cambridge postgraduate applications: the statement covers "reasons for applying", "experience and achievements", "career aspirations" and any "personal circumstances that have affected your academic or other performance" (which cannot be raised later in an appeal); check the course page and "the character or word limit in the Applicant Portal"; "do not repeat information".

Imperial PGT: a five-part frame in order — why this course; relevant experience split into academic background, work/skills, non-academic activities; how the course shapes your career; why Imperial ("particular facilities or research groups you're interested in?"); "a concluding paragraph" that ties it together.
Imperial PGT length: "one or two pages of A4 – that's roughly around 500 to 1,000 words long at font size 12"; Business School instead sets two prompts at 3,500 characters each including spaces.

Imperial PGT opening and focus: avoid "From a young age" / "I have always been interested in"; "We want to hear about you, not us!" — relate course content to your goals rather than praising rankings; check "the right university name and course title".

Warwick WMG: "Aim for between 500 and 1000 words" but "we would very much prefer a more concise and focused essay closer to 500 words"; organise as introduction, body, conclusion; the course selector assesses "how well your goals and objectives align with those of the course".

Warwick WMG register: "full sentences, starting with a capital letter and finishing with a full-stop"; no slang or informal language; short, concise sentences; no "inspirational quotes", no lists, no CV-style content; statements are run through a plagiarism-checking tool and AI-generated ones "tend to be generic in nature and lack authenticity".

Reading careers guidance for postgraduate statements: "around one side of A4 in length, unless otherwise specified"; "Write in paragraphs with a minimum font size of 11 – avoid solid text"; "factual in style rather than descriptive"; the reader may see the statement before the form, so it must stand alone.

Reading order: motivations first as "a short paragraph" that gets "straight to the point" (not "From an early age I've always…"), then why this subject/course/institution (named modules, unique aspects, department specialisms), then what you bring (academic evidence and skills), then career aspirations, then work experience, then extracurricular/positions of responsibility.

UCL GBSH (student-written guidance on the faculty site): the introduction "introduc[es] the programme you're applying for" plus academic background and why postgraduate study; the closing "bring[s] the focus back to your reasons for applying" and reflects on preparation; "Show, don't tell" with a claim-vs-evidence table.
Source (tier): T2 student-authored article on university site (1 Dec 2023)

Rule: University of Galway taught master's: "all applicants must submit/upload a typed personal statement of approximately 600 words" on programme choice and career fit; Business Analytics and Information Systems Management require it "original and unique, maximum 1 A4 page (600 words)"; several programmes waive it.

HKU: "Upload a personal statement of no more than 1000 words detailing your interest in applying to the University, the programme(s), etc." and "You will only be able to submit one personal statement regardless of the number of your programme choice(s)" — so the statement must cover every chosen programme.

University of Otago Master of Teaching and Learning: the personal statement "is required to be in your own handwriting so it will need to be written and then scanned or photographed" and outlines reasons for entering the programme and strengths — the one handwriting requirement found.
Source (tier): T1 College of Education application page

Rule: NUS Psychology graduate (research) programmes: "A typical statement is about 2 pages long"; four parts in order — past research experience, other relevant experience, current research interests, career goals — and the third part must "specify your preferred research area(s), your topics of interest, and at least three individuals with whom you would like to work. Indicate your preferences by rank-ordering these individuals"; contacting them beforehand is invited.

UCT Graduate School of Business (MBA): the "motivations" are answers, not a letter — "Complete each motivation on a separate sheet of paper"; "typed (1.5 line spacing)"; "Each motivation should be between 300 and 400 words"; "Please answer all the questions"; "Give examples where useful".

Wits postgraduate: the "Letter of Motivation" is defined only as a "written statement describing your interest in the programme and the reasons for applying" — no length, form or addressee is published university-wide.

UC Berkeley statement of purpose: a four-part composition in order — (1) "Introduce yourself, your interests and motivations" briefly; (2) research conducted, "with whom, the title of the project, what your responsibilities were, and the outcome. Write technically, or in the style of your discipline"; (3) relevance of recent and current activities; (4) academic interests — "Ideally, pose a question, define a problem, or indicate a theme that you would like to address."

UC Berkeley length: "Approximately 500 to 1,000 well-selected words is better than more words with less clarity and poor organization"; the Personal History Statement "should not duplicate the Statement of Purpose"; check whether the programme requires naming "a professor or professors with whom you might work".

Cornell Academic Statement of Purpose: three moves in order — introduce yourself and your academic interests; describe academic background, preparation and training with specific examples; "Show them you are making an informed decision"; "Unless otherwise noted one to two pages in a standard font and size is typical"; "Include your full name and proposed program of study at the top of each page".

Cornell register: "this is an academically focused essay, not necessarily a personal essay"; "Write with confidence and in an active voice"; naming faculty depends on the programme's ASOP instructions — "determine how best to mention this in your essay".

MIT EECS Communication Lab: open "with a brief portrait of what drives you as a scientist or engineer"; "Close your essay with a 2-3 sentence discussion of your career interests"; "State which professors in the program you would plan to work with. Show how their research areas align with your background and your goals"; "usually no more than 2 pages".

Michigan Rackham formatting: at the top of each document put the document type (Academic Statement of Purpose / Personal Statement), your name, the graduate program name and your 8-digit U-M ID if known; margins at least one inch "so nothing is cropped"; the personal statement has a 500-word limit and "should be different from your Academic Statement of Purpose"; ASOP length is set by the program.

Northwestern TGS: the Academic Statement is "500 to 1,000 words maximum" answering four prompts (interests and reasons; preparation; why this program is the best fit; for research programs, scholarly questions and "name any specific faculty members in this program whose research interests align with your own"); the Personal Statement is "125 to 250 words maximum" and must not duplicate it.

UC San Diego: the statement's first topic is origin — "How did you become interested in this field? Establish that you have had a long-term interest in the field and that you have taken positive steps in pursuing your interest" — and it must "Specifically state your degree objective (Master's or Ph.D.)" and one or two research topics; an explicit invitation to the origin story that UK guidance (M-040, M-044) discourages.

Washington State University History (graduate): avoid "sweeping philosophical generalizations, avowals of political or other ideology" and ruminations on the nature of historical knowledge, and summaries of unrelated extracurriculars; "mention professors with whom you would like to work" is "entirely appropriate, indeed desirable"; "observe word limits strictly"; "The quality of the essay is probably more important than its substantive content".

University of Alberta Education (Studies in Educational Leadership) master's Letter of Intent: "Maximum 2 pages, double-spaced, 12 pt font"; three prompts (how professional experience shaped the interest; questions or challenges in your context; how the programme serves your growth).
Scope: University of Alberta (Faculty of Education, SEL)

Rule: Alberta SEL "What we are NOT looking for": "A summary of your résumé/CV"; "General statements about the value of education"; "Extensive descriptions of courses, faculty members, or information taken from the … website"; "Generic statements that could apply to any graduate program" — the professional-family counterpart to the STEM invitation to name faculty.
Scope: University of Alberta (Faculty of Education, SEL)

Rule: UBC Graduate School statement of interest: "a short essay"; "Connect your area of interest to work being done in the program (mention specific faculty members and projects)"; publications may be cited "in footnotes"; "You are building a case that you are focused, skilled, enthusiastic, and a great match".

Waterloo: the personal statement (also "letter of intent" or "statement of interest") has three elements — interest in the program, tools and skills that will help you succeed, why the program fits you — and "Some programs will have a specific set of prompts/questions for you to answer, but others will not."

KAUST: the statement of purpose is "approximately 750 words" on past work, preparation for the field, relevant background and interests, academic plans, career objectives and reasons for applying — a US-shaped SOP in Saudi Arabia.

Khalifa University: statement of purpose "500-1,000 words" with six recommended points in order — an introduction about yourself, interests and motivations; reasons for the chosen program; what you hope to gain and "any specific issues you wish to address"; professional aspirations; how previous studies and work relate; other relevant matters.

American University of Sharjah: MA TESOL, MAIS and MAMSP require a 600–800-word statement of purpose on motivations, experiences and perspectives, and what the applicant aims to gain — US-shaped essay, UAE.
Source (tier): T1 university InfoDesk article (search excerpt; page returned 403 on direct read)

Rule: University of Tokyo Graduate School of Science (international special selection): two documents — a Personal Statement ("1 or 2 pages of A4-size paper, in English, single space … in any format": what you studied, research conducted, other activities) and a Statement of Purpose (same format: research you wish to conduct, motivations, "if possible, your research plan", "specifying the name(s) of the potential supervising professor(s)"); supervisor contact is a separate required document.
Scope: University of Tokyo (Graduate School of Science)

Rule: University of Tokyo GraSPP MPP/IP: "The length of the statement of purpose must be within 600 words" and it "must include the applicant's motivation to apply for MPP/IP, study plan, and future career implications"; false or plagiarized statements void the application.

Harvard Law School LL.M.: personal statement "no more than 1,500 words — anything exceeding this limit will be disregarded"; footnotes for sources do not count; Part (A) — a legal issue or problem and a framework or strategy to address it — "constituting at least half of the total length"; Part (B) is about the applicant; "solely the product of your own efforts", with disqualification for help from any person or AI.

RISD graduate: "a written statement (500–750 words) outlining your interest and goals in pursuing graduate study"; programme variants override it — Photography wants two statements (statement of purpose ≤750 and "an artist's statement (max. 750 words) that elucidates the work you've included in your submitted portfolio"), Global Arts and Cultures 1,000–2,000 words, Illustration 750–1,500.

CalArts MFA Art: artist statement "between 500 and 1,000 words" addressing "at least three" of the listed questions (inspirations, programme choice, faculty interests, community impact); it contextualises the 20-slide portfolio rather than standing alone.

UCLA Design Media Arts MFA: statement of purpose "up to 500 words"; "You do not need to answer every question"; personal statement also ≤500 words, "approximately 1-page, single spaced, using 1-inch margins and 12-point font".

Fulbright Foreign Student: the Study/Research Objective "should be at least one page and no longer than two pages"; be specific about degree objective, major field and specialised interests; relate to home-country trends and how you will apply the studies on return; a separate Personal Statement (also 1–2 pages) carries the narrative.
Source (tier): T1 IIE essay guidelines (via US Embassy)

Rule: Fulbright Study Objective: "References to proposed universities or faculty should not be made" — the one system that forbids naming a host professor or institution in the fit essay.

Fulbright authorship: "Please use your own words. If you are planning to use someone else's works or research you must credit the source at all times" — citations (APA/MLA/Chicago) are expected inside a scholarship essay, unlike any university letter found.

Australia Awards Scholarships (paper form): the "Supporting statement" is four questions — "Limit your answers to approximately 400 words per question … Please note word limits. Anything over this limit will not be considered" — beginning "Why did you choose your proposed course and institution?" and ending with "up to three practical examples of how you intend to use the knowledge, skills and connections" plus "any possible constraints".
Source (tier): T1 application instructions (Australian High Commission form)
Verified for cycle: form year not printed in extracted text (re-verify)

Rule: Brunei Darussalam Government Scholarship: item 6 "APPLICANT'S STATEMENT OF PURPOSE" is a box on the typed form — "In an essay of up to 200 words, describe your plan of study and/ or research you propose to pursue and relate this to your future career plan" — with additional sheets allowed.

Eiffel (master's): the candidate's "PROJET PROFESSIONNEL … rédigé en français ou, à défaut, en anglais, sur une ou deux pages", explaining the choice of studies in France relative to past studies and future career; institutions submit it, and it may be backed by an external opinion (e.g. an employer).

SNU (Dream Together Master): Form 2 Personal Statement — background, achievements, extracurriculars, volunteer work, employment, reasons for SNU and the programme — has a "3000-Byte limit including spaces and line breaks (approximately 600 English words)"; the Study Plan states academic goals and career aspirations and may include questions to answer and a timeline.

SNU (DTM): "Do NOT include any detailed information regarding your parents and relatives such as names or occupations in the Personal Statement and the Study Plan" — a content prohibition on family origin material.

Tsinghua international master's: "The personal statement should be completed directly in the application system" (a text field, not an upload); a research plan is required of PhD applicants only; programme specifics sit in the catalog's "Remarks of Application".

Zhejiang University (several international master's programmes): personal statement in Chinese or English, "no less than 1500 words", covering study and work experience, reasons for application and a study proposal — a minimum, not a cap.

Ireland long-term study visa: "A signed letter of application, including your full contact details, in English" outlining the reason for coming, family in Ireland/UK/EU, how long you plan to stay, and who bears the cost; a letter, not an essay, and it is read by the visa office, never the university.
Source (tier): T1 Department of Foreign Affairs study visa checklist 2025

Rule: Ireland study visa letter content (ISD guidance): explain "why the educational course you now wish to study does not naturally follow on or relate to your educational or employment history" where that is the case; state that you will observe the conditions of your visa, "will not become a burden on the State" and "will leave the State on the expiry of your permission to remain".
Source (tier): T1 Immigration Service Delivery page (search excerpt; page read truncated)

Rule: New Zealand student visa: a cover letter or statement of purpose is optional and helps show genuine intent; "If you are using an education agent or licensed immigration adviser they cannot write the letter for you"; it may cover why you plan to study in NZ and any later visa plans.
Source (tier): T1 Immigration New Zealand page (search excerpt; URL returned 404 on direct read — locate current page)

Rule: Campus France Études en France: the "motivations" for each formation are a platform text field capped at 1,500 characters, in French, covering parcours, projet d'études (level and field) and projet professionnel; it is read by the Campus France adviser and probed in the entretien pédagogique — not by the university.
Source (tier): T1 Campus France country pages (search excerpts)

Rule: Antwerp IOB Master of Development Studies: the letter must "clearly elaborate on the motivation to attend the programme and how the acquired skills and knowledge will be used upon completion … including a description of future plans and aspirations"; scored under "Selection Criterion 4 (Motivation of the applicant)" as "the ability of the applicant to outline a clear vision on how he/she will make use of the acquired knowledge".

Ghent MSc Global Health: the "personal motivation letter" is three prescribed parts, each "max. 400 words" — a critical reflection on the candidate's field's contribution to Global Health, expectations of the course, and a SWOT analysis positioning the candidate — i.e. a structured essay, not a letter.
Source (tier): T1 programme brochure (search excerpt; page timed out on direct read)

Rule: Where a system publishes nothing on formalities — the UK, North America, Australia/NZ, Singapore, Hong Kong — the document is an essay or portal field with no date, addressee, salutation or signature; the only letter-formality evidence found anywhere is French guidance (M-025), Mexico's UNAM template (M-034), Brazil's UFMG template (M-101), Ireland's visa letter (M-084) and Leiden's pre-printed form (M-016) — i.e. France, Latin America and one visa office.
Source (tier): Synthesis of rows above (finding of absence across ~60 official pages read 2026-09-18)

Rule: HBKU (Qatar) College of Science and Engineering master's: "a personal statement (300-500 words) as part of the online application" explaining why the candidate applies and how the studies serve their objectives, "including information about the applicant's research interests and achievements"; "Personal statements that are incomplete or below the minimum word count will not be accepted" — the only word FLOOR found in any system.

HBKU (other colleges): "a personal statement of interest" that "should introduce the applicant to the Admissions Committee" — topics may include "personal or professional goals and personal, academic, or career history"; "The requirements vary by program" (CHSS); a research proposal is a PhD requirement, not a master's one.
Scope: Hamad Bin Khalifa University (SEM, CHSS, CHLS)

Rule: University of Bahrain postgraduate regulations 2026/27 list no statement, letter or essay among the required documents for master's admission (photo, passport, IELTS, transcripts, recommendation letters, qualification verification) — finding of absence on the university's own regulation.

Malaysia International Scholarship (MIS) 2026: no statement of purpose or motivation letter is among the compulsory documents; a "written research proposal with a minimum of 1,000 words" is required "for Master's by Research and PhD applicants only" and scored on quality and Malaysia relevance; coursework master's submit no narrative document.

Universiti Putra Malaysia postgraduate application: the "Research Proposal" step "will only appear to applicants who have chosen Master by research mode or PhD", with a template provided; no statement is asked of coursework applicants.

Azerbaijan's Heydar Aliyev International Education Grant (2026/27) requires "7. Motivation letter" with no shape rule; documents must be "in one of the following languages: Azerbaijani, Turkish, English and Russian" and notarized — a scholarship letter whose only constraint is language.

Taipei Medical University international master's (fall 2026): two narrative documents — "7. Statement of purpose 讀書計畫" (literally a study plan) and "8. Resume and personal statement 履歷及自傳" (résumé and autobiography) — the Japanese/Korean two-document shape, no length published in the guidelines.

American University in Cairo graduate admission: "a statement of purpose (about 500 words for each graduate program selected) indicating the reasons for interest in the specific program, what you will bring as skills and/or experiences to the program, and how graduate studies fit in your long-term academic and professional objectives"; MIM/CEMS applicants submit "a letter of motivation … instead of a statement of purpose" answering points set in the form.

Cairo University FEPS: the Gender and Development master's requires "a letter explaining the motivation behind enrolling in the program, consisting of 500 words" in English covering motivation, expected goals from the programme and "the future goals of the student in the next five years"; Law and Economics requires "A motivation letter explaining the reason behind joining the program" with no length.

Arba Minch University (Ethiopia) scholarship application form: item "10. MOTIVATION STATEMENT — Please motivate your suitability for receiving this scholarship (Max 250 words)", a box on the form beside a required 3–5-page concept note — the scholarship-form shape (cf. Brunei M-078).

UFMG PPG-GOC (Brazil) "Modelo de Carta de Intenções": a full letter — "Local …, data …", addressed to the "Banca Examinadora" of the programme, a "Ref. Carta de Intenções" line, a fixed opening sentence ("Meu nome é … e venho por meio desta demonstrar interesse…"), boxed sections (academic training, extracurricular, professional activities, justificativa, weekly availability), "Sem mais para o momento, subscrevo-me, Atenciosamente," then name and signature; text outside the boxes is disregarded.

UFRJ Mathematics master's "Carta de Intenções": four numbered questions answered "de maneira sucinta e objetiva" and uploaded as PDF/DOCX — intention and, "Caso já teve contato ou tem interesse em trabalhar com algum professor específico do IM-UFRJ, exponha aqui"; a mathematical result you found interesting; academic events attended; intended area and why. Naming a professor is invited, not required.

USP IME Computer Science master's (2026 edital): the "carta de apresentação (também chamada de carta de motivação ou carta de interesse)" is "de até 2 páginas" and must give (i) research area of interest, (ii) prior educational and extracurricular experience showing aptitude for research, (iii) aims for the programme and after (academic career, industry researcher, entrepreneur), (iv) why this programme over similar ones; align with the programme's research lines and "a disponibilidade de orientadores"; it is weighed within the CV analysis at weight 5 against the exam's weight 3.
USP IME register: "A carta de apresentação deve ser um relato pessoal. O uso de ferramentas assistivas de escrita que usem técnicas de inteligência artificial é fortemente desaconselhado."

PUCP Mathematics master's (Peru): "Una carta de presentación del postulante en formato libre (archivo PDF), explicando su motivación para elegir la Maestría en Matemáticas de la PUCP exponiendo sus conocimientos previos en matemáticas e indicando la línea de investigación en la que desearía trabajar" — free format, PDF, research line named; Statistics, Administrative Law and Human Rights masters ask the same under the names carta de presentación / motivación / interés.

Oxford graduate applications: one upload slot for this document category; "If your course requires both a statement of purpose (or personal statement) and a research proposal, you should submit them within the same document with a clear subheading for each"; "If your statement of purpose or personal statement significantly exceeds the permitted length stated on the relevant course page, it will be removed from your application and your application will be considered incomplete"; an unnecessary statement is removed; departments "may screen your statement of purpose … using plagiarism-detection software".

University of Edinburgh: "around 500 words" with a hard cap of "3,500 characters", entered "directly into the application form"; areas in order — academic history and relevant experience, why Edinburgh, why this programme, career plans; "formal English"; "Copying information from elsewhere, asking someone else to write your statement or using AI apps such as ChatGPT could be considered fraud."

University of Hamburg M.Sc. Intelligent Adaptive Systems: the letter of motivation "accounts for 40% of your ranking score"; "It has to be written by yourself and in English"; "The maximum length is 1.5 pages (not more: the selection committee may reject your application on the grounds of the quality of your motivational letter)"; "Generic or AI generated letters will be rejected!" — the heaviest published weight and the only explicit rejection-for-quality rule found.

Hamburg IAS prescribes an ordered question list the letter must answer — why this programme and which aspects, personal motivation, how it complements existing knowledge, why Hamburg, alignment with goals, "How would you manage cultural adjustment?", and the applicant's own analysis of the selection criteria against the curriculum — a content order that doubles as a rubric.

University of Huddersfield PGT: "around 500 words in a standard 12-point font"; three parts — an introduction explaining interests and what you apply for, a main body "with strong examples of your expertise and skills", a conclusion summarising future goals and motivations; "headings and sub-headings to signpost" are encouraged; avoid contractions, passive voice and AI-generated text; "enthusiastic and professional".

Brunel University: "no more than one side of A4, or around 300 – 500 words"; wants "the specific reasons why you have chosen to study a particular subject and how this is linked to your future goals" and what you contribute; avoid "Repeating information that we can find in the rest of your application", "Being vague", and "Copying any part of your personal statement from another source".

Western Sydney University Master of Research statement of intent: "approximately 250-500 words and does not need to exceed one page"; it must "Identify a potential supervisor(s) who you would like to work with"; "We recommend that you discuss your statement of intent with your proposed supervisor prior to submitting your application"; "Different disciplines have different requirements and expectations".

Qatar University master's: MSc Materials Science and Technology requires "Statement of purpose of minimum 500 words" (a floor, like HBKU's M-091); Master of Accounting a "Short essay stating the candidate's objectives and interests"; MBA, MSc Marketing, MSc Finance and MSc Business Analytics require "Writing a short essay during the personal interview" — composed on the spot, so nothing can be pre-drafted; several master's programmes list no statement at all.

UNU-MERIT / Maastricht MPP: the motivation letter is "roughly 400-500 words", must not repeat the CV, should state "concrete and plausible" short- or medium-term goals and "the value you can bring to the whole MPP cohort"; a separate essay is "1000 words in Word/PDF with searchable text", two parts (problem analysis ≤300 words, policy solution ≤700), "including the use of references" with at least one listed source.

CEU LL.M. in Global Business Law and Regulation: statement of purpose "500 words maximum" on reasons and how the programme serves personal and professional goals; the applicant "may also indicate the topic to which you intend to devote your master's thesis".

Harvard Graduate School of Education Ed.M.: statement of purpose "(1000-word limit)" answering three prompts in order — background ("lived experiences"), objectives for graduate study, fit ("Why is enrollment at HGSE and in your selected Program … critical"); a separate 250-word community prompt; "If you are using quotes or referring to work done by another individual, you should cite your sources … nor will a citation count towards the word limit".
Source (tier): T1 admissions office prompts PDF (rev. 17 Jul 2024)

Rule: RMIT (Australia) Genuine Student Statement of Purpose: "a formal document which states your genuine intent to study in Australia", "required for both Australian student visa (Genuine Student criteria) application and university admissions"; four question areas in order — personal background and academic history, why this course and why RMIT, career goals, why Australia; "responses in your own words"; "Don't forget to sign and date the declaration when finished!" — one document read by both the university and the visa authority.

University of Tokyo Graduate School of Engineering (2027 international master's): the statement is a named form, "AF2_Statement of Study Plans"; "If your application form and submitted documents include any false, misrepresented, or copied statements … (including essays and portfolios prepared by other individuals …), your enrollment may be cancelled, even after entering the school"; a signed Declaration for Applicants is mandatory.
Scope: University of Tokyo (Graduate School of Engineering)

Rule: University of Ghana DASH scholarship (adolescent health): "Personal statement (1 page for master's and 2 pages for PhD applicants), indicating your suitability for a scholarship", with previous research or work experience and career intention in the domain — page limits scaled by level.
